candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Psychosocial Integrity, printed p.10 / PDF p.14
candidate.educational_objective: Use individualized cultural assessment rather than assumptions when planning care.

options.A: Ask the client which cultural beliefs, practices, language needs, or preferences they want incorporated into care.
options.B: Infer likely preferences from the client’s apparent ethnicity so the interview can be shortened.
options.C: Use the same care approach for every client and avoid asking about cultural preferences.
options.D: Delay discussing preferences until a family member can describe the client’s cultural background.

candidate.rationale: Culturally and linguistically appropriate care is individualized. The nurse should ask the client directly about beliefs, practices, language needs, and preferences that matter to care rather than stereotyping from apparent ethnicity or substituting a family member’s assumptions for the client’s own perspective.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CLAS centers respect for the whole individual and tailoring services to the individual’s cultural and language needs and preferences.
candidate.source_locator: What is CLAS? — respect and responsiveness to individual health needs and preferences; tailoring services to culture and language needs
candidate.source_organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Minority Health / Think Cultural Health
candidate.stem: A nurse is beginning care for a client whose cultural background is unfamiliar to the nurse. Which action best supports culturally responsive, individualized care?
